scope: Theorem 9.2 (The comparison through all jets) of the manuscript “Failure of finite assembly for a chromatic overlap at the prime three” (preprints/Failure-of-finite-assembly-for-a-chromatic-overlap-at-the-prime-three-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 318 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b1e58a49eb364dd8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 62. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every m ≥ 1 there is a natural, compatible, J-equivariant quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes D• m −→ C• cts(P, R)[x]/xm , (9.3) where the cochains on R have the finite-stage convention of Definition 3.2. The action of P on the target fixes x, and J acts through its actions on R and the height-two coefficients. Consequently, in each internal degree 2j, the diagonal homotopy cochains of the spectral sequence in Proposition 8.3 are naturally quasi-isomorphic to (︂ lim m C• cts(P, R)[x]/xm )︂ ⊗k[[x]] Ω⊗j . (9.4) Odd internal degrees vanish. In particular, Es,2j 2,∆ = Hs (P, R)[[x]] ⊗k[[x]] Ω⊗j . (9.5) Here the coefficient groups are the actual representations of Theorem 7.13: they are k in degrees 0, 1, the one-dimensional line ℓ in degrees 3, 4, and zero otherwise. The action of J on the first two lines is trivial, and ℓ|O× F = k(δ).
